item.title: The Role of IS Auditors in the Age of AI
item.description:
Artificial intelligence is no longer a futuristic concept — it’s reshaping industries today, and the IS audit profession is no exception. As organizations increasingly adopt AI-driven tools and processes, IS auditors must evolve their skill sets and methodologies to remain effective.

The Changing Landscape

AI is transforming how businesses operate, from automated decision-making to predictive analytics. This transformation introduces new risks: algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, model drift, and the need for explainability. IS auditors must understand these risks to provide meaningful assurance.

item.title: Key Considerations for Banking IT General Controls
item.description:
IT General Controls (ITGC) form the foundation of a bank’s technology control environment. Evaluating these controls requires understanding both the technical landscape and the regulatory context in which banks operate.

Access Management

In banking environments, access management is critical. Auditors should evaluate how user access is provisioned, modified, and deprovisioned. Key areas include privileged access management, role-based access controls, and periodic access reviews. The principle of least privilege should be consistently applied across all systems.

item.title: Getting Started with Cybersecurity Auditing
item.description:
As cyber threats continue to evolve, the demand for cybersecurity auditors is growing rapidly. For traditional IS auditors looking to expand into this domain, here are the essential knowledge areas and skills to develop.

Understand the Threat Landscape

Cybersecurity auditing requires a solid understanding of the threat landscape. This includes knowledge of common attack vectors, threat actors, and the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) they use. Frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK provide a structured way to understand adversary behavior.
